Sample Name: New Patient Evaluation and Medication Coverage
Description: Establishing medication access through the VA while maintaining an outside primary care physician.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: A retired man seeks to arrange medication coverage because his wife's retirement will soon change his insurance benefits. He previously underwent evaluation for Agent Orange exposure but has otherwise received long-term primary care from a community physician for approximately 33 years. He prefers that his outside physician remain the principal coordinator of care while this clinic provides appropriate medication prescriptions, to avoid conflicting orders. He reports no significant acute complaints, exertional chest pain, palpitations, or concerning respiratory symptoms. There is occasional minor cough associated with dry air. He is physically active and reports quitting smoking approximately 20 years ago. Alcohol intake is occasional.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, intermittent back spasm, and an eye disorder treated with drops; additional history to be confirmed from outside records.
MEDICATIONS: Diovan 160 mg once daily, Lipitor, vitamin C, an as-needed muscle relaxant, and daily ophthalmic drops were specifically discussed. The full regimen and doses require correlation with the patient's supplied list.
FAMILY HISTORY: Father with cardiovascular disease, bypass surgery, and probable fatal myocardial infarction; mother with type 2 diabetes; sister with a history of lung cancer.
SOCIAL HISTORY: Retired, former smoker, occasional alcohol use.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Establish a single designated primary physician to coordinate care. Request outside laboratory and medication records, particularly fasting lipid monitoring for statin prescriptions. Discussed colorectal screening options, including yearly stool testing or colonoscopy, within ongoing primary care. Maintain continuity of blood pressure and lipid therapy through coordinated prescribing rather than duplicating clinical management.
